shouldFix.whyItMatters: This artifact's whole method is exact provenance - thirteen governing sources each pinned and, as I verified, each matching live bytes. A field that names file 08 as its measurement source while carrying content only COORD supplies breaks that method at the one place a DR-120 reviewer is most likely to check, since DR-103's standing is what the packaging contract's fixture obligations hang on. A reader auditing the claim against the register will either conclude file 08 was edited when it deliberately was not, or that the artifact mis-measured.

shouldFix.remedy: Either restore faithful row summaries in this field and record the decision-derived standings in a separate field keyed to the COORD digest, or rename/annotate the field to state that standings compose the file-08 row with adopted COORD decisions and cite both digests.

shouldFix.title: archiveProfile claims to own archive determinism but supplies none of its three parameters and routes none of them to a named owner, leaving CI-3's byte-identity promise unbacked
detail: archiveProfile.standing reads 'THIS ARTIFACT OWNS archive determinism. Not canonical JSON. Not ID-DEP-1.' The detachment from canonical JSON is correct and is exactly what Codex CPCV2-B2 asked for; ID-DEP-P1 is correspondingly narrowed to manifests/index only, which I verified.

But the profileRules never state the profile. All three determinism parameters are stated as deferred nouns: 'Member order is A NAMED deterministic order over the tree paths'; 'Timestamps, uid/gid, and uname/gname are normalized to A NAMED zero/omitted profile'; 'Compression, if any, is A NAMED profile token'. No order, profile, or token is named anywhere in the artifact.

Nor are they routed. The fourth rule sends only the packager to OD-P1, and I read both open decisions: OD-P1 is 'Concrete packager, build tool, language toolchain, and command line' and OD-P2 is 'Manifest size caps (schema OD-1)'. Member order, timestamp/ownership normalization and compression token are format-profile parameters distinct from the packager choice, and neither OD covers them. No ID-DEP-P* carries them either.

CI-3 was amended to promise 'same archiveDigest' for identical inputs and to state 'Byte-identical archives ride archiveProfile in this artifact, not canonical JSON / ID-DEP-1.' The ride therefore terminates at a profile with no parameters, so two conforming adapters could emit different archive bytes for the identical committed tree and both satisfy the contract as written.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The artifact elsewhere forbids exactly this shape of gap: the repaired conformanceReport adds lawfulExemptions holding that 'not-applicable and blocked-on-ride are lawful only for a named ride in identityDependencies or namedOpenDecisions. Ungoverned self-exemption is forbidden.' Three unnamed parameters inside the block that claims ownership is the same ungoverned gap, sitting under an operative determinism promise rather than under an exemption.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: The structural half of CPCV2-B2 is genuinely done - archive and archiveDigest are emitted at OC-2, carried at OC-7, produced at S-3-EMIT, excluded from the lock at notALock, and detached from ID-DEP-1. Nothing unsafe is authorized and no false claim is made; the promise is simply not yet dischargeable.
shouldFix.remedy: Name the three tokens in profileRules, or add them to OD-P1's scope or a new OD-P3 with an owner, so CI-3's archive byte-identity rides something that can be evaluated.

That candidate's own schemaContract pins component-manifest-schemas.v11 at 1c0b8868..., which I confirmed is the live v11 digest. The coupling means that if a schemas.v12 is accepted and corpus v3 is re-pointed at it, corpus v3's digest moves and this artifact's citation strands - the identical cycle that has already produced findings against the schema-successor chain. The role text is correctly conservative ('CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. Not SATISFIED-GRADE accepted. Citing it is not an adapter run'), so nothing is overclaimed today. A successor could note the coupling, or cite corpus v3 by named property rather than by whole-document digest alone.
